input.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation: our position is that we retain freedom to source from other suppliers, and this clause also contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3. If some protection is needed, we could accept exclusivity limited to a defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels or delivery dates.

[Playbook] We have deleted the most-favoured-customer obligation running against us; we do not extend our best third-party terms to suppliers, and this conflicts with Section 12.3. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: For twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services, neither Party will solicit for employment any of the other Party's personnel who were directly involved in providing or receiving the Services. This restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at such personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by such personnel, and neither Party is restricted from hiring any person who responds to them.

input.comment: [Playbook] We have narrowed the non-solicit to our fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, limited to personnel involved in the Services, with the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
input.summary: Narrow 12.4 non-solicit to mutual, 12 months, involved personnel, with carve-outs

input.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages payable by us for dependency delays; we do not accept penalties or liquidated damages against the Customer. Vendor's remedy for a genuine Customer-caused delay is relief from the affected schedule and time-and-materials charges for demonstrable standby costs.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: No more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice and during normal business hours, Vendor may audit Customer's usage records through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations. Vendor and its auditor have no right of access, remote or otherwise, to Customer's systems.

input.comment: [Playbook] We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and removed remote access to our systems (consistent with the access limits already in 22.2). Cost allocation in 22.2 is unchanged.
input.summary: Limit audit frequency/notice and delete system access in 22.1

ops.oldText: unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice
ops.newText: unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice

input.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from 180 to 30 days; a six-month window is well outside our position of 30 days (60 days at fallback). The 12-month renewal term and the CPI/3% uplift cap in 8.3 are acceptable as drafted.
input.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice window in 8.2 to 30 days

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains only for-cause and insolvency triggers, so we have added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; we cannot commit to a three-year term with no exit. We can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.
input.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience right as new 9.6
